offence_severity: Minimum/Maximum: 7 years RI under section 201 IPC and death penalty under section 302 IPC
physical_harm: Deceased died on account of head injuries leading to haemorrhage, resultant shock and cardio respiratory failure
number_of_offences: Number of offences/counts charged: 2; Number of offences finally upheld: 0
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the prosecution failed to prove motive, disclosure, recovery, and extra judicial confession beyond reasonable doubt.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as unreliable and shaky, particularly PW4's testimony, which was found full of embellishments and material discrepancies.

legal_representation.accused: Pashupathi Nath Razdan, Mrs. Anuradha Mishra, Vikas Bansal, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Yashraj Singh Deora (Amicus Curiae), Abhishek Singh, Adv.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution relied on the following circumstances: (a) Motive; (b) Disclosure Statement and Recovery; (c) Extra Judicial Confession; and (d) Accused taking the deceased with him and soon thereafter the deceased was found in an injured state.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court was justified in doubting the recovery of blood-stained clothes etc. at the instance of the accused from the hut and on the basis of a disclosure statement made by him. The High Court also found the testimony of PW4 unreliable and shaky.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that reversal of a judgment and order of conviction and acquittal of the accused should not ordinarily be interfered with unless such reversal/acquittal is vitiated by perversity.
precedent_relied_upon: State of U.P. v. Sahai & Others (1982) 1 SCC 352; State of M.P. & Others v. Paltan Mallah & Others (2005) 3 SCC 169; Basheera Begam v. Mohd. Ibrahim & Others (2020) 11 SCC 174
